title: Onboarding and Cost Advisor Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes the Onboarding & Cost Advisor (OCA) product brief and operational playbook for helping customers move from trial usage to predictable consumption on Redwood Inference. The goal of OCA is to reduce time-to-value, lower first-month spend surprises, and provide prescriptive configuration suggestions that map customer workloads to SLO-aligned consumption patterns. This is a product-facing, cross-functional playbook for product, solutions engineering, and customer success teams.

Intended audience:
- Product managers and product marketing
- Solutions engineers and onboarding success
- Platform/infra engineers who operate estimator services
- Sales engineers for demos and proof-of-concept sizing

Goals:
1. Provide deterministic first-30-day cost and latency estimates for common usage patterns (chat, embeddings, reranking).
2. Automate per-route recommendations (batching, quantization profile, cached prefixes) to meet customer SLO targets while minimizing unit cost.
3. Integrate a lightweight UX into Console and Developer Onboarding to show actionable cost trade-offs.
4. Ensure estimator and recommendation APIs are reliable (SLOs defined below) and auditable.

Scope:
- In scope: hosted and dedicated onboarding flows; console integration; SDK-based quick estimator; recommendations for batching, KV cache, quantization presets, and fallback routing policies.
- Out of scope: private (on-prem) air-gapped installations (handled via separate Private Deployment packaging playbook).

Product components (service names):
- consumption-advisor-service: primary recommendation engine (microservice)
- cost-estimator-sdk: client library used in onboarding scripts and web UI
- optimize-conductor (integration): receives recommended quantization and batching profiles and provides rollout plans
- console/route-onramp: Console UI surfaces and onboarding checklist
- capture-proxy: sampling agent for live traffic profiling (opt-in)

Core principles:
- Prescriptive not prescriptive-only: always provide an explanation of each recommendation and safe defaults.
- SLO-first: recommendations must map to explicit latency/cost SLOs provided by the tenant.
- Transparent economics: show per-token/unit cost delta and estimated monthly delta for recommended changes.
- Minimal friction: the estimator should require at most one representative trace (or synthetic sample) to produce an initial plan.

Onboarding flow (step-by-step):
1) Discovery call / baseline capture
   - SE runs a 10–50 request sample using the capture-proxy or uploads a representative prompt set.
   - Required inputs: average prompt length (tokens), expected QPS (requests/sec), target latency SLO per route.
2) Quick estimate (console + SDK)
   - cost-estimator-sdk -> POST /v1/cost/estimate (consumption-advisor-service)
   - Example request body:
     {
       "route": "chat/default",
       "sample_traces": ["base64-encoded-trace"],
       "qps": 5,
       "desired_latency_ms": 250
     }
   - Response includes: monthly_cost_estimate_usd, recommended_batch_size, recommended_quant_profile, confidence_score
3) Prescriptive plan
   - SE reviews recommendations and toggles quick-apply mode (applies only to non-production sandbox routes).
   - For production routes, plan is exported to a canary rollout via optimize-conductor with target % traffic and rollback criteria.
4) Canary and monitoring
   - Canary uses canary-policy: start at 1% traffic for 1 hour, 5% for 4 hours, 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if no regressions.
   - Observe: token cost per 1k, 95th/99th latency, model output quality (sample promptset evals).
5) Acceptance and billing
   - After acceptance, create a consumption estimate card in Console and tag for billing reconciliation.

Integration checklist (quick):
- [ ] Enable capture-proxy for the customer's sandbox environment
- [ ] Install cost-estimator-sdk in demo scripts (npm/pip)
- [ ] Configure client with tenant_id and route mappings
- [ ] Validate recommendations with a 100-request smoke test
- [ ] Add plan to optimize-conductor (if production rollout expected)

Recommendation types and rationale:
- Batching: increase batch size to reduce per-token overhead until latency SLO approaches threshold. Provide expected cost delta and latency impact.
- Quantization profile: prefer Q4_0 or Q4_1 for non-critical routes; full-precision for high-fidelity routes. Include quality delta estimate (% BLEU/synthetic metric delta).
- KV/prefix caching: recommend prefix cache for multi-turn chat when >60% session reuse is observed. Expected cost reduction: 15–40% depending on reuse.
- Fallback routing: route to lower-cost compatible variant when peak capacity would breach SLO; include explicit fallback economics.

SLOs and observability (table-like list):
- consumption-advisor-service availability: 99.95% (target)
- estimator API latency: P95 < 200ms, P99 < 400ms for single-request estimate calls
- recommendation accuracy: 90% of recommended batching/quant profiles should meet predicted cost window +/- 20% in 30-day validation
- canary rollback detection: automatic rollback if 95th latency increases > 20% or model-quality regressions exceed configured thresholds

Metric definitions (what we measure):
- token_unit_cost_usd: unit cost used in estimate
- predicted_monthly_cost_usd: estimator output
- realized_monthly_cost_usd: post-rollout billing reconciliation target
- recommendation_confidence: 0.0 - 1.0 scoring that drives quick-apply UX

UX patterns and Console flows:
- Onboarding banner: prompt to run quick estimate with recommended inputs (tokens, qps, target latency).
- Diff view: side-by-side compare of current route config vs recommended config with cost delta and latency delta.
- Explainability panel: natural-language justification for each recommendation and link to relevant docs (quantization-profiles, batching-guidelines).

Rollout plan and acceptance criteria:
- Beta (Q3 2026): feature available to select ramp customers; collect telemetry for 30 days. Beta acceptance requires: estimator P95 <200ms, recommendation_confidence >= 0.7 for 75% of evaluations, and mean absolute % error < 30% vs realized costs.
- GA (Q4 2026): enable self-serve quick estimate in Console; add billing tagging and consumption cards. GA acceptance: production SLA, automated reconciliation path in finance.

Security and data privacy:
- Sample traces must be scrubbed by default: PII redaction rules applied in capture-proxy. Customers must opt into full-trace uploads.
- Estimator service logs only aggregated metrics; raw traces stored only if customer opts in and signs processing agreement.

Operational runbook (summary):
- On incident for consumption-advisor-service:
  1. Pager to eng-platform on P1 (service down)
  2. Toggle fallback: UI should present precomputed safe-default recommendations via static policy (route: "safe-default")
  3. Postmortem: include metric divergence analysis (predicted vs realized) and refine estimator model

Rollout metrics (tracked weekly):
- number_of_estimates_run
- percent_of_customers_with_active_plan
- delta_monthly_cost_estimate_vs_realized (median, 75th, 95th percentiles)
- adoption_rate_of_recommendations (applied vs suggested)

Example API (cost-estimator-sdk) - minimal request/response (JSON):
Request:
{
  "tenant_id": "redwood-acme-42",
  "routes": [
    {
      "name": "chat/default",
      "sample_tokens_avg": 420,
      "qps": 4,
      "latency_target_ms": 250
    }
  ],
  "time_window_days": 30
}

Response:
{
  "predicted_monthly_cost_usd": 1245.72,
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "route": "chat/default",
      "batch_size": 4,
      "quant_profile": "Q4_0",
      "expected_cost_delta_pct": -28.2,
      "confidence": 0.82
    }
  ],
  "explainers": ["Batching reduces host overhead for short sequences; Q4_0 gives ~2-3x perf improvement for this model family with minor quality impact"]
}

Billing reconciliation notes:
- Tag all applied recommendations with recommendation_id and plan_id in billing events to reconcile predicted vs realized costs. Finance will run a monthly reconciliation job that compares predicted_monthly_cost_usd vs realized_monthly_cost_usd and report exceptions >10%.

Known limitations and next steps:
- Quality estimation: current quality delta estimates use synthetic similarity and may under/overestimate real-world degradation for domain-specific prompts. Next step: integrate tenant-provided evaluation prompt sets into accuracy pipeline.
- Private deployments: plan packaging for on-prem customers is a Q1 2027 dependency.
- Multi-route interactions: recommendations currently assume independent routes; work planned to model cross-route batching effects.

Release notes (summary):
- 2026-07-28 (published): Initial GA playbook and console quick-estimator UX. Beta customers: Acme Retail, Finex Analytics. Known caveat: quantization confidence requires additional validation on domain-specific datasets.

Appendix:
- Quick CLI example (using cost-estimator-cli):
  cost-estimator-cli estimate --tenant redwood-acme-42 --route chat/default --qps 4 --tokens 420 --latency 250

- Helpful references:
  - Quantization profiles guide: /product-docs/design-specs/quality-aware-quantization-rollout-prd-2026-12-01
  - Canary rollout playbook: /product-docs/design-specs/progressive-variant-rollouts-compatibility-matrix-spec-2026.json

If you own an onboarding plan or are running an SE engagement, use this playbook as the canonical steps and update the plan_id tag in the Console when you start a canary. For product questions, contact the product owner listed above.
